title: Isolate egress label leak that causes intermittent cross-tenant DNS cache hits
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
A small subset of Dedicated clusters has seen intermittent cross-tenant DNS cache hits after control-plane rebalances and router path changes. The result is transient DNS responses that resolve private service names from a different tenant under high churn. Multiple enterprise customers escalated (notably Acme Health and FinSight) after observing private hostnames returned in client-facing logs.

Observed behavior and telemetry:
- Spike in resolver error reports and privacy alerts starting 2026-03-03; correlated with node rebalances and peering route churn events.
- Affected requests show egress proxy label reuse: ephemeral proxy label (constructed from host+path) was being reassigned to a different tenant before existing per-label DNS cache entries expired.
- KV cache + DNS TTL mismatch: cached A/AAAA responses lingered under the reused label namespace, causing requests from the new tenant to hit stale DNS entries.
- Failure windows are short (30s-3min) but reproducible in staging with controlled peering flaps.

Reproduction steps (staging):
1. Provision a dedicated pool with two tenant namespaces and enable VPC peering to the same external resolver.
2. Seed DNS cache by making resolver calls from tenant A to private.hostname.internal.
3. Trigger router reassign/rebalance to move egress path from node X to node Y (simulate network flap).
4. Immediately make identical resolver calls from tenant B; observe that responses occasionally match tenant A's cached results.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by debugging):
- Egress label assignment currently encodes ephemeral properties but is not strictly namespaced by tenant when recycled quickly during path failover.
- When a label is reused, we do not atomically invalidate or namespace-share DNS cache entries per-tenant; the DNS cache is keyed by label and resolver tuple, so reuse allows cross-tenant hits.
- Under heavy rebalancing, connection tracking entries (conntrack) and proxy label lifecycles become out of sync, leaving a window where label -> cached DNS mapping is valid but now associated with the wrong tenant.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- Toggle A: Force single-path egress (disable multipath) for affected Dedicated pools via control-plane flag to stop label churn (rollback safe). Applied to two impacted fleets on 2026-03-06; reduced customer reports by ~90%.
- Toggle B: Short-term DNS cache TTL clamp per-ephemeral-label to 5s for newly-assigned labels to reduce exposure window.

Proposed permanent fix (implementation plan):
1) Label scoping change (server-side): modify label allocator to include tenant ID as a mandatory prefix in the ephemeral label namespace. This prevents label reuse across tenants unless explicitly shared. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821)
2) Atomic cache invalidation: on label reassignment, emit a label-deprecation event that triggers immediate DNS cache invalidation for the old label-->resolver keys.
3) Conntrack cleanup: ensure conntrack entries are flushed for the old label on failover and make cleanup idempotent across controllers.
4) Add invariants and unit tests to the egress label allocator and DNS cache to assert tenant affinity.

Rollout plan and monitoring:
- Canary (2026-03-13): Deploy label scoping and cache invalidation to 5% of Dedicated capacity in a low-risk region. Monitor metrics: cross-tenant-dns-alerts, resolver-5xx-rate, tenant-isolation-violations (custom metric).
- Ramp to 25% after 6h if no regression, full rollout in 48h.
- Post-deploy verification: run repro harness (automated peering-flap) in canary and validate no cross-tenant DNS hits.
- Rollback: Flip scoping flag off and re-enable single-path egress if any privacy regressions observed.

QA and validation:
- Test harness updated in infra-tests repo to simulate peering flaps and assert no DNS cross-tenant leakage. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Dedicated+Egress+Labeling+Postmortem)
- Staging run completed 2026-03-09 with synthetic load; observed elimination of reproducer in 35/36 runs.

Follow-ups and outstanding items:
- Postmortem write-up and customer communication draft (owner: Maya Chen).
- Add an SLO and alert for label-reuse anomalies.
- Audit other cache layers (prefix/KV cache) for similar label-key assumptions.
- Backfill changelog and mention under runtime-2.4.1 release notes.

Artifacts and links:
- Hotfix PR (TTL clamp): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4789
- Permanent fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Staging repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/compare/egress-label-harness
